key_insight: Apply a strong sustainability lens to AI: maintain critical natural capital by constraining and redesigning AI’s energy, material and lifecycle impacts rather than assuming technological substitution will solve ecological limits.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between fast-growing AI compute/material demands and planetary boundaries by providing a framework that accounts for embodied impacts, ecological thresholds and governance mechanisms to avoid overshoot.
method: Develop a conceptual framework that translates 'strong sustainability' principles into AI development choices (protect natural capital, non-substitutability of critical ecosystems).
Propose measurable lifecycle metrics and accounting (embodied materials, supply-chain emissions, energy use) and scenario analysis to assess ecological footprint of AI trajectories.

Outline technical and policy interventions (e.g., design-for-efficiency, circular hardware, caps or allocation systems, procurement rules, and governance instruments) to align AI growth with ecological limits.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners concrete priorities—measure lifecycle impacts, favour efficiency and reuse, and design within ecological constraints—while informing policy and organisational choices that prevent environmental overshoot.
visual_elements: Lifecycle Sankey diagram showing energy and material flows for model training, deployment and hardware production.
Side-by-side comparison graphic: Weak vs Strong Sustainability (what can/cannot be substituted and policy implications).
Time-series chart: projected compute growth vs planetary boundary thresholds (scenarios with and without interventions).
Icon grid of interventions: efficiency, circular hardware, governance (caps/allocations), and procurement standards.
paper_title: A strong sustainability approach to AI development
